This prequalification process aims to identify Economic Operators with proven expertise in the planning, production, implementation and integration of such devices in accordance with applicable technical and regulatory requirements. title-proc.eng: Portable and modular unmanned aircraft detection and tracking system

description-proc.eng: As part of its commitment to advanced sustainable aviation, Oulu University of Applied Sciences seeks a reliable and innovative portable and modular unmanned aircraft detection and tracking system (hereafter referred to as the system) tailored to its needs. The system to be procured will support the research, development, and training initiatives at Oulu University of Applied Sciences. The system must be able to enhance aviation safety, for example near airports, city centres, and other areas where safe flying is crucial. The system must be a portable and modular solution suitable for continuous operation in demanding weather and field conditions. The system must enable Radio Frequency-based detection of drones operating on commonly used drone frequencies. The system must provide a map-based, real-time situational awareness view and must be capable of logging detected events in a reliable and verifiable manner. The system must include a standardised and encrypted interface for external integrations. The system must support remote access, but it must also be capable of fully autonomous operation without network connectivity in field conditions. The system must include the antenna with mounting structures, necessary cabling, and a processing unit. The system must be quick to deploy and install by two persons, and its design must support easy portability and redeployment. The procurement is co-funded by the Council of Oulu Region, European Regional Development Fund (ERDF), Dronelogistics Service Point project (A81394). The procurement is dependent on an extension of the implementation period granted for the project. The procurement contract will be signed with the selected supplier if the funder grants the extension. The decision on the extension is expected in June 2026. The possession, import, and use of devices intended for radio interference require a radio license granted in advance by the Finnish Transport and Communications Agency (Traficom). Therefore, the supply contract will be signed with the selected supplier provided that Traficom grants the required radio license to the contracting entity.

title-proc.eng: Acquisition of Desert Boots to the Danish Defence

description-proc.eng: The Danish Ministry of Defence Acquisition and Logistics Organisation (DALO) wishes to renew the framework agreements concerning the military Combat Boot system. The system consists of 7 framework agreements including specific boots and an assortment of various related footwear whereas this Contract Notice covers the Desert Boots. The Desert Boot is part of the soldier’s equipment. Without boots that fits ergonomically, and/or suit the environment, the soldier cannot perform to the best of his/her abilities. Therefore this tender aims to provide each soldier (male and female) with boots, that fit the soldiers individually and provide the necessary protection in different environments. The Desert Boot will be used by soldiers working in offices most of their time, but the Desert Boot shall also function as a boot for use in dry warm desert areas. It is important that the Desert Boot is breathable, light, flexible and has shock absorption in the midsole. But at the same time provides enough stability to the foot and ankle. The Desert Boot must have a lifetime of minimum 12 months of military use. To fully understand the requirements of the Desert Boot see Appendix 1 in the tendering material. The evaluation of the boots includes tests of products samples. description-proc.fra: Avec cet avis d’information préalable (PIN), Elia souhaite partager ses plans autour du produit Power System Model et mieux comprendre ce que le marché peut offrir. À ce stade, nous ne définissons pas encore de solution fixe, mais explorons plutôt les approches, outils et expériences possibles. L’objectif principal est de recueillir les avis des fournisseurs potentiels sur la manière dont ils relèveraient ce type de défi, quelles solutions existent déjà et ce qui a prouvé son efficacité dans des contextes comparables. Cela aidera Elia à valider son orientation, à affiner ses exigences et à faire des choix plus éclairés avant de lancer un appel d’offres officiel. Pour Elia, cette étape est importante pour réduire les risques, éviter de négliger les solutions pertinentes et garantir que les marchés futurs soient réalistes et alignés sur ce que le marché peut offrir. Elia s’appuie actuellement sur plusieurs modèles de données de grille pour soutenir des décisions cruciales telles que les investissements, la maintenance, les opérations de marché et la sécurité. L’organisation évolue vers une approche plus harmonisée et intégrée de la gestion des modèles de données en grille, réduisant la fragmentation et améliorant la cohérence, la prise de responsabilité et la prise de décision entre les cas d’usage À mesure que le paysage énergétique évolue — avec une électrification rapide, une intégration accrue des énergies renouvelables et des contraintes croissantes du réseau — le besoin de modèles de données précis, évolutifs et harmonisés devient de plus en plus crucial. La taille et la complexité du modèle de grille augmentent considérablement, tant au niveau national que par les interactions transfrontalières, tandis que le nombre et la fréquence des calculs continuent de croître. Pour relever ces défis, Elia transforme son approche de gestion des données grâce au programme d’optimisation des données sur le cycle de vie des actifs (ALC DO) et une transition vers la propriété des données basée sur le produit, incluant le développement d’un produit modèle réseau. L’objectif du produit du modèle système électrique est de permettre un modèle unifié, de haute qualité et évolutif, qui consolide et expose les paramètres électriques nécessaires aux calculs du système. Ce modèle garantira la cohérence, soutiendra un large éventail de cas d’utilisation opérationnels et analytiques, et agira comme une source de données maîtresse certifiée pour des éléments clés tels que les ressources système, les états de fonctionnement et les limites — permettant ainsi une prise de décision plus rapide, plus fiable et basée sur les données.
description-proc.deu: Mit dieser Frühzeitmitteilung (PIN) möchte Elia seine Pläne rund um das Power System Model Product teilen und besser verstehen, was der Markt zu bieten hat. In dieser Phase definieren wir noch keine feste Lösung, sondern erkunden vielmehr mögliche Ansätze, Werkzeuge und Erfahrungen. Das Hauptziel ist es, Rückmeldungen potenzieller Lieferanten zu sammeln, wie sie diese Art von Herausforderung angehen würden, welche Lösungen es bereits gibt und was sich in vergleichbaren Kontexten bewährt hat. Dies wird Elia helfen, seine Richtung zu validieren, seine Anforderungen zu schärfen und fundiertere Entscheidungen zu treffen, bevor eine formelle Ausschreibung gestartet wird. Für Elia ist dieser Schritt wichtig, um Risiken zu reduzieren, relevante Lösungen nicht zu übersehen und sicherzustellen, dass die zukünftige Beschaffung realistisch und mit dem übereinstimmt, was der Markt bieten kann. Elia verlässt sich derzeit auf mehrere Netzdatenmodelle, um kritische Entscheidungen wie Investitionen, Wartung, Marktbetrieb und Sicherheit zu unterstützen. Die Organisation bewegt sich zu einem harmonisierteren und integrierteren Ansatz zur Verwaltung von Grid-Datenmodellen, wodurch Fragmentierung reduziert und Konsistenz, Eigenverantwortung und Entscheidungsfindung über Anwendungsfälle hinweg verbessert werden Mit der Entwicklung der Energielandschaft – mit schneller Elektrifizierung, verstärkter Integration erneuerbarer Energien und wachsenden Netzbeschränkungen – wird der Bedarf an genauen, skalierbaren und harmonisierten Datenmodellen immer kritischer. Größe und Komplexität des Grid-Modells nehmen sowohl im Inland als auch durch grenzüberschreitende Interaktionen erheblich zu, während Anzahl und Häufigkeit der Berechnungen weiterhin zunehmen. Um diese Herausforderungen zu bewältigen, überarbeitet Elia seinen Datenmanagementansatz durch das Asset Lifecycle Data Optimization (ALC DO)-Programm und einen Wandel hin zum produktbasierten Dateneigentum, einschließlich der Entwicklung eines Network Model Product. Das Ziel des Power System Model Product ist es, ein einheitliches, hochwertiges und skalierbares Modell zu ermöglichen, das elektrische Parameter konsolidiert und offenlegt, die für Systemberechnungen erforderlich sind. Dieses Modell gewährleistet Konsistenz, unterstützt eine breite Palette operativer und analytischer Anwendungsfälle und dient als zertifizierte Masterdatenquelle für Schlüsselelemente wie Systemressourcen, Betriebszustände und Grenzen – was letztlich eine schnellere, zuverlässigere und datengetriebene Entscheidungsfindung ermöglicht.
description-proc.nld: Met deze Prior Information Notice (PIN) wil Elia zijn plannen rond het Power System Model Product delen en beter begrijpen wat de markt te bieden heeft. Het belangrijkste doel is om input te verzamelen van potentiële leveranciers over hoe zij dit soort uitdagingen zouden aanpakken, welke oplossingen er al bestaan en wat goed heeft gebleken in vergelijkbare contexten. Dit zal Elia helpen haar koers te valideren, haar eisen aan te scherpen en beter geïnformeerde keuzes te maken voordat een formele aanbesteding wordt gelanceerd. Voor Elia is deze stap belangrijk om het risico te verminderen, relevante oplossingen niet over het hoofd te zien en ervoor te zorgen dat de toekomstige inkoop realistisch is en in lijn met wat de markt kan leveren. Elia vertrouwt momenteel op meerdere griddatamodellen om kritieke beslissingen te ondersteunen, zoals investeringen, onderhoud, marktoperaties en veiligheid. De organisatie beweegt zich richting een meer geharmoniseerde en geïntegreerde aanpak voor het beheren van grid data-modellen, waarbij fragmentatie wordt verminderd en consistentie, eigendom en besluitvorming over use cases heen wordt verbeterd. Naarmate het energielandschap zich ontwikkelt—met snelle elektrificatie, toegenomen integratie van hernieuwbare energie en toenemende netwerkbeperkingen—wordt de behoefte aan nauwkeurige, schaalbare en geharmoniseerde datamodellen steeds belangrijker. De omvang en complexiteit van het gridmodel breiden zich aanzienlijk uit, zowel nationaal als via grensoverschrijdende interacties, terwijl het aantal en de frequentie van berekeningen blijven toenemen. Om deze uitdagingen aan te pakken, transformeert Elia zijn datamanagementbenadering via het Asset Lifecycle Data Optimization (ALC DO)-programma en een verschuiving naar productgebaseerd data-eigendom, inclusief de ontwikkeling van een Network Model Product. Het doel van het Power System Model Product is het mogelijk maken van een uniform, hoogvarig en schaalbaar model dat elektrische parameters consolideert en blootlegt die nodig zijn voor systeemberekeningen. Dit model zorgt voor consistentie, ondersteunt een breed scala aan operationele en analytische gebruiksscenario's en fungeert als een gecertificeerde masterdatabron voor belangrijke elementen zoals systeembronnen, operationele toestanden en limieten—waardoor uiteindelijk snellere, betrouwbaardere en datagedreven besluitvorming mogelijk wordt.
description-proc.eng: With this Prior Information Notice (PIN), Elia wants to share its plans around the Power System Model Product and better understand what the market can offer. At this stage, we are not yet defining a fixed solution, but rather exploring possible approaches, tools, and experiences available. The main goal is to gather input from potential suppliers on how they would tackle this type of challenge, what solutions already exist, and what has proven to work well in comparable contexts. This will help Elia validate its direction, sharpen its requirements, and make more informed choices before launching a formal tender. For Elia, this step is important to reduce risk, avoid overlooking relevant solutions, and ensure that the future procurement is realistic and aligned with what the market can deliver. Elia currently relies on multiple grid data models to support critical decisions such as investments, maintenance, market operations, and safety. The organization is moving towards a more harmonized and integrated approach to managing grid data models, reducing fragmentation and improving consistency, ownership and decision making across use cases As the energy landscape evolves—with rapid electrification, increased renewable integration, and growing network constraints—the need for accurate, scalable, and harmonized data models becomes more critical. The size and complexity of the grid model are expanding significantly, both domestically and through cross-border interactions, while the number and frequency of calculations continue to grow. To address these challenges, Elia is transforming its data management approach through the Asset Lifecycle Data Optimization (ALC DO) program and a shift towards product-based data ownership, including the development of a Network Model Product. The objective of the Power System Model Product is to enable a unified, high-quality, and scalable model that consolidates and exposes electrical parameters required for system calculations. This model will ensure consistency, support a wide range of operational and analytical use cases, and act as a certified master data source for key elements such as system resources, operating states, and limits—ultimately enabling faster, more reliable, and data-driven decision-making.

In the previous contract, a framework was developed to assess the acceptable variation within each characteriser of a Nanoform (as per Section 2.4 of Annex VI of REACH Regulation). The project aimed at exploring ways to simplify nanoforms registration process and, ultimately, its’ associated testing burden. As an outcome, a series of binary decision trees and respective variability threshold were produced, covering each mandatory characteriser. The framework was developed based on a limited set of information covering metallic and carbon-based nanomaterials. The final report as well as the Decision Tree can be found here: https://echa.europa.eu/fi/science/publications-and-reports/reports, so that interested parties can already familiarize themselves with the outcome of the project. The new contract aims at refining the threshold values pre-established and validating it with additional data sets, covering a wider range of chemical types. The project outcome is expected to become a basis for ECHA to develop new guidance for registrants of nanoforms of a substance.

title-proc.eng: Framework Agreement for the Delivery of Control Systems (IEC104) and the Provision of related services

description-proc.eng: Framework Agreement for the Delivery of Control Systems (IEC104) and the Provision of related services TenneT is a leading European transmission system operator responsible for the safe and reliable transmission of electrical energy over long distances. TenneT’s core tasks include the expansion and maintenance of the transmission grid, the integration of renewable energy sources, and the assurance of grid stability. TenneT’s grid area covers large parts of Germany and the Netherlands and includes both onshore and offshore connections. As an operator of critical infrastructure, the security and reliability of the systems in use are of particular importance. The aim of this tender is the establishment of two framework agreements for the procurement of substation Control Systems, in particular Intelligent Electronic Devices (IEDs) and field control units, for use in TenneT TSO GmbH’s (TTG) high‑voltage and extra‑high‑voltage substations. The systems to be procured are intended for control, monitoring, signalling and automation purposes within substations and are a key element of secure and reliable grid operation. Within the scope of this tender, TTG intends to procure Control System components including, but not limited to, bay control units, station control units, interface devices, and related auxiliary equipment. A central focus of the procurement is the use of the communication protocol IEC 60870‑5‑104 (IEC 104) for the exchange of control, status and measurement data between the substation level and higher‑level control systems. The devices shall support typical substation automation functions, reliable IEC 104 communication, and seamless integration into existing station control concepts in accordance with applicable technical standards. The subject of this tender is the supply of Control Systems hardware, including IEDs and associated components, as well as related documentation and services necessary for commissioning and integration into TTG’s substations. The framework agreement shall enable TTG to call off devices on demand over the contract term for new installations, refurbishments, and replacement purposes. Parallel to the hardware framework agreement, TTG intends to conclude a separate service contract covering the maintenance of the devices and the maintenance of embedded software, including corrective and preventive measures as well as software updates and upgrades, in accordance with the contractual provisions. Due to increasing requirements regarding system availability and redundancy, the procurement procedure is structured into two lots, which will be awarded separately. The lot structure is intended to ensure supply security, operational resilience and redundancy of the Control Systems deployed within TTG’s transmission grid. TenneT TSO GmbH is certified according to ISO 27001. Therefore, only Control Systems and equipment that comply with TTG’s Operational Technology security requirements may be offered (OT security and IT security requirements).
